record.paper_title: Progresses on some open problems related to infinitely many symmetries
record.original_question: Why do some integrable systems appear to be missing generalized symmetries of certain orders, such as the absence of order 6n + 3 symmetries in the Sawada-Kotera and Kaup-Kupershmidt equations, and more generally can even-order or fractional-order generalized symmetries exist for standard integrable equations such as KdV and modified KdV?

evidence.quote:
Open problem 4: Loss of certain orders of generalized symmetries
The existence of an infinitely many symmetries with varying orders in integrable systems is well-documented. However, for certain key integrable systems, specific orders of generalized symmetries appear to be absent. For instance, the Sawada-Kortera (SK) [11] and Kaup-Kupershmidt (KK) [12] equations exhibit generalized symmetries of orders 6n + 1 and 6n + 5 (n = 0, 1, . . . , ∞), yet the 6n + 3 order symmetries are missing. Furthermore, for well-known equations like KdV and MKdV, there are infinitely many generalized symmetries of odd orders. This raises the question of the existence of even order symmetries and, more broadly, the possibility of fractional order symmetries.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Consider an evolution equation u_t = K(u, u_x, u_{xx}, ...) for a scalar function u(x,t). A generalized (Lie–Bäcklund) symmetry is a vector field whose characteristic Q(x,t,u,u_x,u_{xx},...,u_{(n)}) satisfies the linearized equation D_t Q = K'[Q], where K' is the Fréchet derivative of K and D_t is taken along solutions. The order of the symmetry is the highest order of x-derivatives of u appearing in Q. An equation is said to possess an infinite hierarchy of generalized symmetries when there are infinitely many such Q of unbounded orders.

It is known that:
(a) The Sawada–Kotera equation u_t = u_{xxxxx} + 5 u u_{xxx} + 5 u_x u_{xx} + 5 u^2 u_x and the Kaup–Kupershmidt equation u_t = u_{xxxxx} + 10 u u_{xxx} + 25 u_x u_{xx} + 20 u^2 u_x both admit infinite hierarchies of generalized symmetries of orders 6n+1 and 6n+5 for n = 0, 1, 2, ..., while no generalized symmetry of order 6n+3 has been exhibited.
(b) The KdV equation u_t = u_{xxx} + 6 u u_x and the modified KdV equation u_t = u_{xxx} + 6 u^2 u_x admit infinitely many generalized symmetries of odd orders, while no generalized symmetry of even order has been exhibited.

Problems.
1. Prove or disprove the existence of generalized symmetries of order 6n+3 (n ∈ ℕ) for the Sawada–Kotera and Kaup–Kupershmidt equations, and explain rigorously the structural mechanism that obstructs (or permits) them.
2. Prove or disprove the existence of any even-order generalized symmetry for the KdV and modified KdV equations.
3. Formulate a precise notion of "fractional-order generalized symmetry" (e.g., via pseudodifferential symbols, nonlocal recursion operators, or Riemann–Liouville/Caputo-type fractional derivatives in x), and determine whether the KdV, modified KdV, Sawada–Kotera, and Kaup–Kupershmidt equations admit nontrivial generalized symmetries of fractional order under such a definition.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work that proves the absence of order 6n+3 symmetries for Sawada–Kotera/Kaup–Kupershmidt or that establishes (non)existence of even-order symmetries for KdV/mKdV, nor a definitive theory of fractional-order generalized symmetries for these systems. The question is posed as a current open problem in the surveying source, and no resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Multipotentializations and nonlocal symmetries: Kupershmidt, Kaup-Kupershmidt and Sawada-Kotera equations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses nonlocal symmetries and potentializations connecting Sawada–Kotera, Kaup–Kupershmidt, and Kupershmidt equations, but does not address the missing 6n+3 order symmetries or even/fractional-order symmetries for KdV/mKdV.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature studies symmetries of these equations but does not resolve the missing-order question.
